checks.message: KMS encryption not configured for SNS topic
checks.context: SNS topics without KMS encryption store messages in plaintext. For topics carrying sensitive data (PII, financial records), enable server-side encryption with a customer managed KMS key.

checks.message: Review topic policy for wildcard principals
checks.context: An SNS topic policy with Principal:* allows any AWS account to publish or subscribe. This can be exploited to inject malicious messages or subscribe to sensitive notifications.

checks.message: SNS subscription using unencrypted HTTP endpoint
checks.context: HTTP subscriptions transmit SNS messages in plaintext, exposing message content and enabling man-in-the-middle attacks. Use HTTPS endpoints only.

checks.message: Topic deletion removes all subscriptions permanently
checks.context: Deleting an SNS topic immediately removes all subscriptions. Any publishers sending to this topic ARN will receive errors. Subscribers will stop receiving notifications without warning.

checks.message: KMS encryption not configured for SQS queue
checks.context: SQS queues without server-side encryption store messages in plaintext. For queues carrying sensitive data, enable SSE with a KMS key using the KmsMasterKeyId attribute.

checks.message: Review queue policy for wildcard principals
checks.context: An SQS queue policy with Principal:* allows any AWS account to send or receive messages. This can be exploited to inject malicious messages or drain the queue. Scope access to specific principals.

checks.message: Queue deletion is permanent — all unprocessed messages will be lost
checks.context: Deleting an SQS queue is immediate and irreversible — all messages in it are destroyed, including those not yet processed. You must wait 60 seconds before creating a new queue with the same name.

checks.message: Queue purge deletes ALL messages permanently
checks.context: PurgeQueue deletes every message in the queue immediately. This cannot be undone. Ensure this is intentional and that no critical unprocessed messages will be lost.

checks.message: Removing a subscription silently stops notifications to that endpoint
checks.context: If the subscription delivers security alerts, billing notifications, or operational alarms, removing it creates a blind spot. Verify no critical monitoring depends on this subscription.

checks.message: Verify the permission does not grant access to untrusted accounts or use wildcard actions
checks.context: SQS add-permission adds a statement to the queue policy. A statement with Principal: * or Action: SQS:* allows any AWS account to send or receive messages. Use set-queue-attributes with a full policy document for more granular control.

checks.message: Verify messages are deleted after processing to prevent duplicate processing
checks.context: SQS messages are not deleted after receive — they become invisible for the visibility timeout period. If your consumer fails to delete the message, it reappears and is processed again. Ensure your consumer calls delete-message after successful processing.

checks.message: Verify the permission does not grant publish access to untrusted accounts
checks.context: SNS add-permission adds a statement to the topic policy. Granting Publish to an untrusted account allows them to inject messages into your topic, potentially triggering downstream Lambda functions, SQS queues, or HTTP endpoints with malicious payloads.

checks.message: Verify the message does not contain plaintext secrets or PII
checks.context: SNS messages are delivered to all subscribers and may be logged in CloudTrail. Messages containing credentials, API keys, or PII are exposed to all subscribers and anyone with CloudTrail read access. Use references to Secrets Manager ARNs instead of actual secret values.
